page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.32-128 is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the Ampere Altra processor platform. It runs on the 64-bit Arm (arm64) architecture, featuring 32 dedicated physical CPU cores clocked at 3.0 GHz. Unlike simultaneous multithreading designs, the processor provides exactly one hardware thread per core, totaling 32 vCPUs without resource sharing across hyperthreads. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, establishing a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per physical core.

This server type does not bundle local NVMe or solid-state storage, requiring networked block storage volumes for system boot and data persistence. Graphic processing units are absent from the hardware profile, with zero GPUs provisioned. For external connectivity, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure allocates one complimentary public IPv4 address to the instance.

The dedicated single-thread-per-core design ensures predictable compute throughput and eliminates noisy-neighbor side effects common in hyperthreaded environments. The balanced allocation of memory and processing units makes this Arm-based instance highly resource-efficient for horizontally scalable software architectures. Tradeoffs include the requirement to run Arm-compatible application binaries and reliance on network-attached storage for disk operations. VM.Standard.A1.Flex.32-128 is suited for microservices deployments, container orchestration nodes, continuous integration and build pipelines, web application serving, and backend database services ported to aarch64.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.32-128 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the Ampere Altra processor family. Operating on the 64-bit Arm architecture, this configuration provides 32 dedicated physical cores running at a fixed 3.0 GHz frequency, with one thread per core avoiding hyperthreading contention. It is provisioned with 128.0 GB of system memory, matching a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and operates without onboard local storage, requiring remote block volumes for persistence. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs allocated. The single-threaded core design delivers linear compute scaling and consistent execution timing across concurrent threads. This profile achieves high resource efficiency for horizontally scaled Linux environments. VM.Standard.A1.Flex.32-128 is well-matched for web application hosting, API gateways, continuous integration builds, microservices clusters, and general enterprise workloads targeting the aarch64 ecosystem.
